snippet: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: O Sañjaya, after my sons and the sons of Pāṇḍu assembled in the place of pilgrimage at Kurukṣetra, desiring to fight, what did they do?
reflection: Where in my life am I behaving like Dhṛtarāṣṭra — protecting 'my' side instead of dharma?

snippet: Sañjaya said: O King, after looking over the army arranged in military formation by the sons of Pāṇḍu, King Duryodhana went to his teacher and spoke the following words.
reflection: Have I approached a teacher or mentor recently with a hidden agenda?

snippet: O my teacher, behold the great army of the sons of Pāṇḍu, so expertly arranged by your intelligent disciple the son of Drupada.
reflection: Where am I avoiding the truth of someone else's spiritual strength?

snippet: Here in this army are many heroic bowmen equal in fighting to Bhīma and Arjuna: great fighters like Yuyudhāna, Virāṭa and Drupada.
reflection: Whom in my life am I overlooking as a quiet warrior of dharma?

snippet: There are also great heroic, powerful fighters like Dhṛṣṭaketu, Cekitāna, Kāśirāja, Purujit, Kuntibhoja and Śaibya.
reflection: Whose association is silently shaping me, and into whose image?

snippet: There are the mighty Yudhāmanyu, the very powerful Uttamaujā, the son of Subhadrā and the sons of Draupadī. All these warriors are great chariot fighters.
reflection: Am I building community, or only consuming it?

snippet: But for your information, O best of the brāhmaṇas, let me tell you about the captains who are especially qualified to lead my military force.
reflection: What am I pretending not to know about my own situation?

snippet: There are personalities like you, Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Kṛpa, Aśvatthāmā, Vikarṇa and the son of Somadatta called Bhūriśravā, who are always victorious in battle.
reflection: Where am I confusing inherited custom with eternal dharma?

snippet: There are many other heroes who are prepared to lay down their lives for my sake. All of them are well equipped with different kinds of weapons, and all are experienced in military science.
reflection: What loyalties of mine are quietly transactional?

snippet: Our strength is immeasurable, and we are perfectly protected by Grandfather Bhīṣma, whereas the strength of the Pāṇḍavas, carefully protected by Bhīma, is limited.
reflection: Where am I impressed by quantity when I should be evaluating quality?

snippet: All of you must now give full support to Grandfather Bhīṣma, as you stand at your respective strategic points of entrance into the phalanx of the army.
reflection: Whom am I leaning on heavily — and is that leaning surrender, or avoidance?

snippet: Then Bhīṣma, the great valiant grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, the grandfather of the fighters, blew his conchshell very loudly, making a sound like the roar of a lion, giving Duryodhana joy.
reflection: Whose 'conch' do I rally to when I am bewildered?

snippet: After that, the conchshells, drums, bugles, trumpets and horns were all suddenly sounded, and the combined sound was tumultuous.
reflection: What sound vibrations dominate my mornings — devotional or distracting?

snippet: On the other side, both Lord Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, stationed on a great chariot drawn by white horses, sounded their transcendental conchshells.
reflection: When I serve, am I aware of Kṛṣṇa as my companion, or only as my employer?

snippet: Lord Kṛṣṇa blew His conchshell, called Pāñcajanya; Arjuna blew his, the Devadatta; and Bhīma, the voracious eater and performer of herculean tasks, blew his terrific conchshell, called Pauṇḍra.
reflection: What is the unique shape of the service I am called to render?

snippet: King Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, blew his conchshell, the Ananta-vijaya, and Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka. That great archer the King of Kāśī, the great fighter Śikhaṇḍī, Dhṛṣṭadyumna,…
reflection: Where do I disqualify myself from collective service because my role feels small?

snippet: The blowing of these different conchshells became uproarious. Vibrating both in the sky and on the earth, it shattered the hearts of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
reflection: Where am I exhausting myself in argument when sincere practice would be the louder testimony?

snippet: At that time Arjuna, the son of Pāṇḍu, seated in the chariot bearing the flag marked with Hanumān, took up his bow and prepared to shoot his arrows. O King, after looking at the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra drawn in military…
reflection: What duty have I been quietly postponing?

snippet: Arjuna said: O infallible one, please draw my chariot between the two armies so that I may see those present here, who desire to fight, and with whom I must contend in this great trial of arms.
reflection: Have I asked Kṛṣṇa, today, to give me clear vision over my present situation?

snippet: Let me see those who have come here to fight, wishing to please the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
reflection: What in my life am I refusing to actually see?

snippet: Sañjaya said: O descendant of Bharata, having thus been addressed by Arjuna, Lord Kṛṣṇa drew up the fine chariot in the midst of the armies of both parties.
reflection: Whose hands are on the reins of my life right now — mine, or Kṛṣṇa's?

snippet: In the presence of Bhīṣma, Droṇa and all the other chieftains of the world, the Lord said, “Just behold, Pārtha, all the Kurus assembled here.”
reflection: Where has Kṛṣṇa positioned me precisely so that I must finally face something?

snippet: There Arjuna could see, within the midst of the armies of both parties, his fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, and also his fathers-in-law and well-wishers.
reflection: Whose faces, lined up before me, would shake my resolve to act in dharma?

snippet: When the son of Kuntī, Arjuna, saw all these different grades of friends and relatives, he became overwhelmed with compassion and spoke thus.
reflection: Where is my 'compassion' actually a refusal to do what dharma requires?

snippet: Arjuna said: My dear Kṛṣṇa, seeing my friends and relatives present before me in such a fighting spirit, I feel the limbs of my body quivering and my mouth drying up.
reflection: When did I last feel my limbs shake at the weight of a real choice?

snippet: My whole body is trembling, my hair is standing on end, my bow Gāṇḍīva is slipping from my hand, and my skin is burning.
reflection: Where is my body telling me what my mind refuses to admit?

snippet: I am now unable to stand here any longer. I am forgetting myself, and my mind is reeling. I see only causes of misfortune, O Kṛṣṇa, killer of the Keśī demon.
reflection: Where in my life has the bow already slipped, and I am pretending it is still in my hand?

snippet: I do not see how any good can come from killing my own kinsmen in this battle, nor can I, my dear Kṛṣṇa, desire any subsequent victory, kingdom or happiness.
reflection: What 'victory' would no longer taste sweet to me, even if I won it?

snippet: O Govinda, of what avail to us are a kingdom, happiness or even life itself when all those for whom we may desire them are now arrayed on this battlefield? O Madhusūdana, when teachers, fathers, sons, grandfathers,…
reflection: Which of my 'renunciations' are actually just preferences in disguise?

snippet: Sin will overcome us if we slay such aggressors. Therefore it is not proper for us to kill the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and our friends. What should we gain, O Kṛṣṇa, husband of the goddess of fortune, and how could we be…
reflection: Where am I dressing up sentiment as conscience?

snippet: O Janārdana, although these men, their hearts overtaken by greed, see no fault in killing one’s family or quarreling with friends, why should we, who can see the crime in destroying a family, engage in these acts of sin?
reflection: Where am I waiting for collective consensus to do what is already individually clear?

snippet: With the destruction of the dynasty, the eternal family tradition is vanquished, and thus the rest of the family becomes involved in irreligion.
reflection: Which spiritual structures in my life are quietly eroding?

snippet: When irreligion is prominent in the family, O Kṛṣṇa, the women of the family become polluted, and from the degradation of womanhood, O descendant of Vṛṣṇi, comes unwanted progeny.
reflection: Where have we kept the form of family but lost its dharma?

snippet: An increase of unwanted population certainly causes hellish life both for the family and for those who destroy the family tradition. The ancestors of such corrupt families fall down, because the performances for…
reflection: What does my environment communicate to the women in it about their spiritual worth?

snippet: By the evil deeds of those who destroy the family tradition and thus give rise to unwanted children, all kinds of community projects and family welfare activities are devastated.
reflection: How am I caring for the lineage of souls that came before me?

snippet: O Kṛṣṇa, maintainer of the people, I have heard by disciplic succession that those whose family traditions are destroyed dwell always in hell.
reflection: Where am I trying to force everyone into one mold rather than honoring different natures?

snippet: Alas, how strange it is that we are preparing to commit greatly sinful acts. Driven by the desire to enjoy royal happiness, we are intent on killing our own kinsmen.
reflection: What decision am I about to make whose consequences I have not weighed seriously?

snippet: Better for me if the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, weapons in hand, were to kill me unarmed and unresisting on the battlefield.
reflection: Which of my hard lines are dharmic, and which are merely dramatic?

snippet: Sañjaya said: Arjuna, having thus spoken on the battlefield, cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.
reflection: Where has the bow fallen from my hand in this season of life?

snippet: Sañjaya said: Seeing Arjuna full of compassion, his mind depressed, his eyes full of tears, Madhusūdana, Kṛṣṇa, spoke the following words.
reflection: Whose 'compassion' am I admiring that may actually be ignorance of the soul?

snippet: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear Arjuna, how have these impurities come upon you? They are not at all befitting a man who knows the value of life. They lead not to higher planets but to infamy.
reflection: Whom in my life do I expect to console me when I actually need correction?

snippet: O son of Pṛthā, do not yield to this degrading impotence. It does not become you. Give up such petty weakness of heart and arise, O chastiser of the enemy.
reflection: What is my 'strength-name' that I have forgotten in this season?

snippet: Arjuna said: O killer of enemies, O killer of Madhu, how can I counterattack with arrows in battle men like Bhīṣma and Droṇa, who are worthy of my worship?
reflection: What honest objections am I withholding from Krishna?

snippet: It would be better to live in this world by begging than to live at the cost of the lives of great souls who are my teachers. Even though desiring worldly gain, they are superiors. If they are killed, everything we…
reflection: Which of my noble-sounding instincts may still be missing the highest dharma?

snippet: Nor do we know which is better – conquering them or being conquered by them. If we killed the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, we should not care to live. Yet they are now standing before us on the battlefield.
reflection: Where is my honest uncertainty more truthful than my confident answers?

snippet: Now I am confused about my duty and have lost all composure because of miserly weakness. In this condition I am asking You to tell me for certain what is best for me. Now I am Your disciple, and a soul surrendered…
reflection: Where in my life have I claimed independence that I should hand back?

snippet: I can find no means to drive away this grief which is drying up my senses. I will not be able to dispel it even if I win a prosperous, unrivaled kingdom on earth with sovereignty like the demigods in heaven.
reflection: What material remedy am I still chasing for a problem only Krishna can resolve?

snippet: Sañjaya said: Having spoken thus, Arjuna, chastiser of enemies, told Kṛṣṇa, “Govinda, I shall not fight,” and fell silent.
reflection: Where am I filling space with words that I should be filling with listening?

snippet: O descendant of Bharata, at that time Kṛṣṇa, smiling, in the midst of both the armies, spoke the following words to the grief-stricken Arjuna.
reflection: Have I felt Krishna's affectionate smile in my struggles, or only my own anxiety?

snippet: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: While speaking learned words, you are mourning for what is not worthy of grief. Those who are wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead.
reflection: What am I lamenting that the wise would not lament?

snippet: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.
reflection: When do I most forget my own eternal nature?

snippet: As the embodied soul continuously passes, in this body, from boyhood to youth to old age, the soul similarly passes into another body at death. A sober person is not bewildered by such a change.
reflection: Where do I still treat the body's transitions as if they were my own annihilation?

snippet: O son of Kuntī, the nonpermanent appearance of happiness and distress, and their disappearance in due course, are like the appearance and disappearance of winter and summer seasons. They arise from sense perception,…
reflection: Which discomfort am I treating as permanent that is actually only a season?

snippet: O best among men [Arjuna], the person who is not disturbed by happiness and distress and is steady in both is certainly eligible for liberation.
reflection: What does my disturbance reveal about what I am still attached to?

snippet: Those who are seers of the truth have concluded that of the nonexistent [the material body] there is no endurance and of the eternal [the soul] there is no change. This they have concluded by studying the nature of both.
reflection: Where am I still pouring real effort into the asat?

snippet: That which pervades the entire body you should know to be indestructible. No one is able to destroy that imperishable soul.
reflection: What fears would dissolve if I really felt the indestructibility of the soul?

snippet: The material body of the indestructible, immeasurable and eternal living entity is sure to come to an end; therefore, fight, O descendant of Bharata.
reflection: What am I treating as ultimate that is actually only temporary?

snippet: Neither he who thinks the living entity the slayer nor he who thinks it slain is in knowledge, for the self slays not nor is slain.
reflection: What am I carrying credit or blame for that the soul never truly did?

snippet: For the soul there is neither birth nor death at any time. He has not come into being, does not come into being, and will not come into being. He is unborn, eternal, ever-existing and primeval. He is not slain when…
reflection: Where is my behavior contradicting my belief in the soul's eternity?

snippet: O Pārtha, how can a person who knows that the soul is indestructible, eternal, unborn and immutable kill anyone or cause anyone to kill?
reflection: How would my reactions change if I truly knew the soul is unkillable?

snippet: As a person puts on new garments, giving up old ones, the soul similarly accepts new material bodies, giving up the old and useless ones.
reflection: Whose 'changing of clothes' am I still grieving as if it were total loss?

snippet: The soul can never be cut to pieces by any weapon, nor burned by fire, nor moistened by water, nor withered by the wind.
reflection: Which 'weapon, fire, water, or wind' am I most afraid of right now?

snippet: This individual soul is unbreakable and insoluble, and can be neither burned nor dried. He is everlasting, present everywhere, unchangeable, immovable and eternally the same.
reflection: What in me is genuinely immutable — and how often do I reside there?

snippet: It is said that the soul is invisible, inconceivable and immutable. Knowing this, you should not grieve for the body.
reflection: Where am I demanding that spiritual truth submit to material measurement?

snippet: If, however, you think that the soul [or the symptoms of life] will always be born and die forever, you still have no reason to lament, O mighty-armed.
reflection: Even from a purely material view, what am I lamenting that has no rational basis?

snippet: One who has taken his birth is sure to die, and after death one is sure to take birth again. Therefore, in the unavoidable discharge of your duty, you should not lament.
reflection: What inevitability am I exhausting myself trying to deny?

snippet: All created beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their interim state, and unmanifest again when annihilated. So what need is there for lamentation?
reflection: What in my middle-section life would I cherish more if I really accepted its brevity?

snippet: Some look on the soul as amazing, some describe him as amazing, and some hear of him as amazing, while others, even after hearing about him, cannot understand him at all.
reflection: How much of my 'knowledge' of the soul is mere hearing without realization?

snippet: O descendant of Bharata, he who dwells in the body can never be slain. Therefore you need not grieve for any living being.
reflection: How can I hold both the truth of eternity and the duty of compassion at once?

snippet: Considering your specific duty as a kṣatriya, you should know that there is no better engagement for you than fighting on religious principles; and so there is no need for hesitation.
reflection: What is my sva-dharma in this stage of life — and am I performing it without apology?

snippet: O Pārtha, happy are the kṣatriyas to whom such fighting opportunities come unsought, opening for them the doors of the heavenly planets.
reflection: What unsought opportunity is currently in front of me that I am hesitating over?

snippet: If, however, you do not perform your religious duty of fighting, then you will certainly incur sins for neglecting your duties and thus lose your reputation as a fighter.
reflection: Where am I about to abandon a dharma because of how it will look?

snippet: People will always speak of your infamy, and for a respectable person, dishonor is worse than death.
reflection: Which decision in my recent past would I be ashamed to recount in twenty years?

snippet: The great generals who have highly esteemed your name and fame will think that you have left the battlefield out of fear only, and thus they will consider you insignificant.
reflection: Whose worst suspicion of me am I about to confirm by avoidance?

snippet: Your enemies will describe you in many unkind words and scorn your ability. What could be more painful for you?
reflection: What ridicule am I avoiding by sacrificing dharma?

snippet: O son of Kuntī, either you will be killed on the battlefield and attain the heavenly planets, or you will conquer and enjoy the earthly kingdom. Therefore, get up with determination and fight.
reflection: Where am I refusing to commit because I am calculating the cost?

snippet: Do thou fight for the sake of fighting, without considering happiness or distress, loss or gain, victory or defeat – and by so doing you shall never incur sin.
reflection: Which choice am I weighing by emotional comfort that should be weighed by dharma?

snippet: Thus far I have described this knowledge to you through analytical study. Now listen as I explain it in terms of working without fruitive results. O son of Pṛthā, when you act in such knowledge you can free yourself…
reflection: Where is my knowledge running ahead of my practice?

snippet: In this endeavor there is no loss or diminution, and a little advancement on this path can protect one from the most dangerous type of fear.
reflection: What 'small' practice have I been dismissing that may already be protecting me?

snippet: Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is many-branched.
reflection: What is the one resolute aim of my life — am I living as if I have one?

snippet: Men of small knowledge are very much attached to the flowery words of the Vedas, which recommend various fruitive activities for elevation to heavenly planets, resultant good birth, power, and so forth. Being…
reflection: Whose flowery promises have I been entertaining lately?

snippet: In the minds of those who are too attached to sense enjoyment and material opulence, and who are bewildered by such things, the resolute determination for devotional service to the Supreme Lord does not take place.
reflection: What enjoyment is keeping my intelligence from being firmly fixed?

snippet: The Vedas deal mainly with the subject of the three modes of material nature. O Arjuna, become transcendental to these three modes. Be free from all dualities and from all anxieties for gain and safety, and be…
reflection: Which guṇa is currently dominating my consciousness, and how do I know?

snippet: All purposes served by a small well can at once be served by a great reservoir of water. Similarly, all the purposes of the Vedas can be served to one who knows the purpose behind them.
reflection: Which rituals do I cling to that have lost their living purpose for me?

snippet: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of action. Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities, and never be attached to not doing your duty.
reflection: Which 'fruit' am I most secretly attached to in my work?

snippet: Perform your duty equipoised, O Arjuna, abandoning all attachment to success or failure. Such equanimity is called yoga.
reflection: Where do I lose samatva most easily — and what does that reveal?

snippet: O Dhanañjaya, keep all abominable activities far distant by devotional service, and in that consciousness surrender unto the Lord. Those who want to enjoy the fruits of their work are misers.
reflection: Where am I being a miser with the results of my actions?

snippet: A man engaged in devotional service rids himself of both good and bad reactions even in this life. Therefore strive for yoga, which is the art of all work.
reflection: Where could I bring more skill (kauśalam) into my daily action as yoga?

snippet: By thus engaging in devotional service to the Lord, great sages or devotees free themselves from the results of work in the material world. In this way they become free from the cycle of birth and death and attain…
reflection: What recent 'fruit' have I privately savored that I should formally offer?

snippet: When your intelligence has passed out of the dense forest of delusion, you shall become indifferent to all that has been heard and all that is to be heard.
reflection: What is my own forest of delusion right now, and what am I doing to cross it?

snippet: When your mind is no longer disturbed by the flowery language of the Vedas, and when it remains fixed in the trance of self-realization, then you will have attained the divine consciousness.
reflection: Where is my mind still moved by promises and preferences I claim to have outgrown?

snippet: Arjuna said: O Kṛṣṇa, what are the symptoms of one whose consciousness is thus merged in transcendence? How does he speak, and what is his language? How does he sit, and how does he walk?
reflection: What does the conduct of the sthita-prajña look like in modern life?

snippet: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O Pārtha, when a man gives up all varieties of desire for sense gratification, which arise from mental concoction, and when his mind, thus purified, finds satisfaction in the…
reflection: Which desires occupy my mind that, when honest, I would not want to fulfill?

snippet: One who is not disturbed in mind even amidst the threefold miseries or elated when there is happiness, and who is free from attachment, fear and anger, is called a sage of steady mind.
reflection: Which of the three — attachment, fear, anger — owns me most often?

snippet: In the material world, one who is unaffected by whatever good or evil he may obtain, neither praising it nor despising it, is firmly fixed in perfect knowledge.
reflection: Where am I addicted to celebration or lamentation as a form of identity?

snippet: One who is able to withdraw his senses from sense objects, as the tortoise draws its limbs within the shell, is firmly fixed in perfect consciousness.
reflection: Which sense most frequently drags me out of the shell of remembrance?

snippet: Though the embodied soul may be restricted from sense enjoyment, the taste for sense objects remains. But, ceasing such engagements by experiencing a higher taste, he is fixed in consciousness.
reflection: Which lingering rasa (taste) of mine has not actually been replaced, only suppressed?

snippet: The senses are so strong and impetuous, O Arjuna, that they forcibly carry away the mind even of a man of discrimination who is endeavoring to control them.
reflection: Which 'turbulent sense' has surprised me by overpowering me recently?

snippet: One who restrains his senses, keeping them under full control, and fixes his consciousness upon Me, is known as a man of steady intelligence.
reflection: Where am I fighting senses head-on instead of fixing on Krishna?

snippet: While contemplating the objects of the senses, a person develops attachment for them, and from such attachment lust develops, and from lust anger arises.
reflection: What did I contemplate yesterday that ripened into attachment today?

snippet: From anger, complete delusion arises, and from delusion bewilderment of memory. When memory is bewildered, intelligence is lost, and when intelligence is lost one falls down again into the material pool.
reflection: Where has anger recently bewildered my memory of who I really am?

snippet: But a person free from all attachment and aversion and able to control his senses through regulative principles of freedom can obtain the complete mercy of the Lord.
reflection: Where is my 'spiritual life' an avoidance rather than a disciplined engagement?

snippet: For one thus satisfied [in Kṛṣṇa consciousness], the threefold miseries of material existence exist no longer; in such satisfied consciousness, one’s intelligence is soon well established.
reflection: What sorrows of mine have not been destroyed because tranquillity has not been established?

snippet: One who is not connected with the Supreme [in Kṛṣṇa consciousness] can have neither transcendental intelligence nor a steady mind, without which there is no possibility of peace. And how can there be any happiness…
reflection: Which link in this chain is currently broken in me?

snippet: As a strong wind sweeps away a boat on the water, even one of the roaming senses on which the mind focuses can carry away a man’s intelligence.
reflection: Which 'wandering sense' has most often blown my boat off course?

snippet: Therefore, O mighty-armed, one whose senses are restrained from their objects is certainly of steady intelligence.
reflection: Which sense, if more restrained, would most strengthen my buddhi?

snippet: What is night for all beings is the time of awakening for the self-controlled; and the time of awakening for all beings is night for the introspective sage.
reflection: What am I 'awake' to that the world is asleep to?

snippet: A person who is not disturbed by the incessant flow of desires – that enter like rivers into the ocean, which is ever being filled but is always still – can alone achieve peace, and not the man who strives to satisfy…
reflection: Am I trying to be a desert when Krishna asks me to be an ocean?

snippet: A person who has given up all desires for sense gratification, who lives free from desires, who has given up all sense of proprietorship and is devoid of false ego – he alone can attain real peace.
reflection: What 'mine' is most quietly costing me my peace?

snippet: That is the way of the spiritual and godly life, after attaining which a man is not bewildered. If one is thus situated even at the hour of death, one can enter into the kingdom of God.
reflection: Am I living as if the brāhmī state is something I will actually attain?

snippet: Arjuna said: O Janārdana, O Keśava, why do You want to engage me in this ghastly warfare, if You think that intelligence is better than fruitive work?
reflection: Where am I frozen between two seemingly conflicting good paths?

snippet: My intelligence is bewildered by Your equivocal instructions. Therefore, please tell me decisively which will be most beneficial for me.
reflection: Which authentic confusion am I hiding under intellectual gymnastics?

snippet: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O sinless Arjuna, I have already explained that there are two classes of men who try to realize the self. Some are inclined to understand it by empirical, philosophical…
reflection: Which path does my actual nature call me to right now?

snippet: Not by merely abstaining from work can one achieve freedom from reaction, nor by renunciation alone can one attain perfection.
reflection: Where am I calling avoidance 'detachment'?

snippet: Everyone is forced to act helplessly according to the qualities he has acquired from the modes of material nature; therefore no one can refrain from doing something, not even for a moment.
reflection: What invisible 'doings' of mine deserve more conscious offering?

snippet: One who restrains the senses of action but whose mind dwells on sense objects certainly deludes himself and is called a pretender.
reflection: Where is my outward restraint hiding inner indulgence?

snippet: On the other hand, if a sincere person tries to control the active senses by the mind and begins karma-yoga [in Kṛṣṇa consciousness] without attachment, he is by far superior.
reflection: Where am I being too pristine to be genuinely useful?

snippet: Perform your prescribed duty, for doing so is better than not working. One cannot even maintain one’s physical body without work.
reflection: What 'dropping out' fantasy is keeping me from my actual duty?

snippet: Work done as a sacrifice for Viṣṇu has to be performed; otherwise work causes bondage in this material world. Therefore, O son of Kuntī, perform your prescribed duties for His satisfaction, and in that way you will…
reflection: Which of my daily activities are still being done for myself rather than for Kṛṣṇa?

snippet: In the beginning of creation, the Lord of all creatures sent forth generations of men and demigods, along with sacrifices for Viṣṇu, and blessed them by saying, “Be thou happy by this yajña [sacrifice] because its…
reflection: What in my life today is sacrificed, and what is merely consumed?

snippet: The demigods, being pleased by sacrifices, will also please you, and thus, by cooperation between men and demigods, prosperity will reign for all.
reflection: What gifts of nature do I take without acknowledgement?

snippet: In charge of the various necessities of life, the demigods, being satisfied by the performance of yajña [sacrifice], will supply all necessities to you. But he who enjoys such gifts without offering them to the…
reflection: Where in my life am I quietly stealing — taking without offering back?

snippet: The devotees of the Lord are released from all kinds of sins because they eat food which is offered first for sacrifice. Others, who prepare food for personal sense enjoyment, verily eat only sin.

reflection: What devotee-audience could I share with?

snippet: There is no servant in this world more dear to Me than he, nor will there ever be one more dear.
reflection: Has Kṛṣṇa's love motivated me as much as my own preferences?

snippet: And I declare that he who studies this sacred conversation of ours worships Me by his intelligence.
reflection: Have I been reading like ordinary literature?

snippet: And one who listens with faith and without envy becomes free from sinful reactions and attains to the auspicious planets where the pious dwell.
reflection: What audio practice could I add?

snippet: O son of Pṛthā, O conqueror of wealth, have you heard this with an attentive mind? And are your ignorance and illusions now dispelled?
reflection: What confusion has the Gītā dispelled in me?

snippet: Arjuna said: My dear Kṛṣṇa, O infallible one, my illusion is now gone. I have regained my memory by Your mercy. I am now firm and free from doubt and am prepared to act according to Your instructions.
reflection: What of Arjuna's response can I genuinely speak as my own?

snippet: Sañjaya said: Thus have I heard the conversation of two great souls, Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna. And so wonderful is that message that my hair is standing on end.
reflection: When did sacred conversation last give me goosebumps?

snippet: By the mercy of Vyāsa, I have heard these most confidential talks directly from the master of all mysticism, Kṛṣṇa, who was speaking personally to Arjuna.
reflection: Whose mercy am I receiving the Gītā through?

snippet: O King, as I repeatedly recall this wondrous and holy dialogue between Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna, I take pleasure, being thrilled at every moment.
reflection: When did I last rejoice over a verse I've read many times?

snippet: O King, as I remember the wonderful form of Lord Kṛṣṇa, I am struck with wonder more and more, and I rejoice again and again.
reflection: When did wonder last fade for me?

snippet: Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the master of all mystics, and wherever there is Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will also certainly be opulence, victory, extraordinary power, and morality. That is my opinion.
reflection: Where have I doubted that Kṛṣṇa + sincere effort wins?
